Output: Quality and relevance of higher education services (teaching, research, extension) enhanced Indicator: 50 grants will be allocated under the newly established competitive research fund Achievement: 201 Progress/Status: Completed.
A total of 201 research proposals were submitted in Q1-Q2/2020 but only 52 proposals were selected and awarded. Of the 52 research, 22 research results will be used for teaching and learning and will be uploaded to LUMS for knowledge sharing among universities. Eleven research project reports were published in local journals: Journal of National University of Laos and Souphanouvong University Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development. 29 research project reports are waiting for endorsement to be published in those local journals. Two research reports were published in international academic journals: International Journal of Environmental and Rural Development and International Journal of Politics, Law and Management. Six research project reports have been submitted to international journals for validation and publication. Four research projects will be further developed and improved for production. Those development include digital fire alarm system, bio-fertilizer and bio-pesticides from Lao strains microorganism using biotechnology, development of gas fruit production, milk drinking products from purple rice. Four research results are being submitted for patent registration. Data Source: MOES project and HEI reports, LUMS, published articles

Output: Access to modern higher education programs introduced Indicator: New 3,700 student capacity Savannakhet University campus, including classrooms, laboratories, education resource center, administration facilities available for use; other campus infrastructure designed. Progress/Status: Civil works completed.
Package CW1, comprising construction of linguistics and engineering faculty buildings and related MEP infrastructure, was awarded on 1 Apr 2020 and completed in 2022.
CW4 ($8.5 million) included a faculty building (IT), Tech cluster, student dormitory, landscaping for both core and non-core campus areas, miscellaneous facilities (covered walkway), and MEP infrastructure. Package was awarded in January 2021 and completed in June 2023.
Package CW6 (construction of science faculty building) and CW7 (construction of food science faculty building) was awarded in February 2022 and completed in December 2023.
Civil works 5, comprising procurement of fixtures and furniture for SKU, was signed on 23 January 2023. It was installed and completed in December 2023.
CW8, which will construct the SKU sports facility, was awarded in December 2022 and completed in June 2023. Additional works were completed in December 2023.
Additional minor civil works for construction of NUOL's fertilizer house (CW13) and refurbishment of SU's science laboratory have been approved. The construction was completed in December 2023.
Data on student capacity ongoing consolidation. Data Source: MOES project reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management of HEIs strengthened Indicator: 200 senior managers, governors, MOES staff, and academic leaders of participating HEIs will receive capacity building and mentoring in leadership, strategic management, and institutional planning Progress/Status: Completed.
As of 30 September 2023, the project financed several training programs as part of institutional capacity building for a total of 312 participants, including 103 (31%) women. (i) A total of 171 university managers, faculty heads, and senior academic and administrative staff attended training on governance and management reform through webinars. The universities are inputting staff profile and student information on examination, scores, and financial information into the LUMS which is hoped to improve the university governance and management; (ii) trained 141 (31% female) senior managers and academic staff on data survey. With the training, they can conduct tracer studies and employer survey, analyze the data and prepare reports. The results are being used to prepare their enrollment plans and coordinate with private sector to ensure their courses will be matched with the skills needed. Data Source: MOES project capacity-building records Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Number of higher education (university) enrollments increases to 45,000 Achievement: 28873 Progress/Status: Not met.
As of academic year (AY) 2022/23, enrolment for the four universities is at 28,873, even below the baseline, of whom 14,358 (50%) were women. The female target of 45% has been achieved but the overall decline will lead to this outcome not being achieved. Reasons for the decline in enrollment are as follows over the years: • AY 2017/2019: decreased enrollment in business and administration because of over labor supply in this area. • AY 2019/2020: about 1/3 of secondary graduates entered the work forces, particular migrant to work as unskilled workers in Thailand; and COVID-19 impact. • AY 2020/21 - 2022/23: less job opportunities, skills mismatch and financial difficulties. Data Source: LUMS

Number of higher education (university) enrollments increases to 45% women Achievement: 45 Progress/Status: Completed.

12 memorandums of understanding (contracts) signed by MOES and HEIs to provide extension and consultancy services (job placements, applied research, among others) Achievement: 29 Progress/Status: Completed.
Twenty nine (29) MOAs were signed with 11 partner universities for matching scholarships under the project; (ii) through MOAs with the DHE, the four universities received various consultancy services from 15 visiting scholars who provided them guidance on governance and leadership, industry engagement, research, networking, and instructional delivery improvement and various other topics—leading them to partner with industry partners and universities; (iii) 18 MOAs signed in 2022—to establish partnership with industries in varying degrees of engagement on curriculum development, joint academic activities, practical training and internships, training for teaching staff and students and seminars, supply of equipment, joint research and faculty management; which are expected jump start university-industry engagement to produce quality instruction and increased employability of students. Data Source: HEI financial reports Baseline value: n/a
